subject: Operator credential rotation & standby swarm plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Connors <sara.connors@aurumhealth.com>, security@aurumhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Operator credential rotation & standby swarm plan

Hi Sara / Aurum Security team,

Thanks for the list of concerns in the RFI. Attached are three artifacts that address your operational control questions for on-prem/VPC and air-gapped installs: a credential rotation matrix (operator_rotation_matrix.xlsx), the standby swarm runbook (standby_swarm_runbook_v2.pdf), and the access approval form (access-approval-form.docx).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Credential rotation cadence: default 90-day for non-privileged operators; 30-day for break-glass emergency operator accounts; support for policy-driven rotation via customer KMS or our HSM gateway.
- Standby swarm: a light-weight operator group model we use for minimal-ops sites where an on-call "swarm" can be escalated and given time-limited access tokens (15m–8h) scoped via vault leases.
- Maintenance & evacuation: documented operator de-provisioning and physical escort/escrow procedures are in section 4 of the runbook.

Key asks from you to finalize:
1) Preferred maximum emergency window for break-glass access (we propose 4 hours default).
2) Whether you require operator account creation / rotation to be fully mirrored in your IdP (SAML SCIM) or if you prefer a KMS-wrapped token workflow.
3) Any blackout windows (weekly maintenance windows, regulatory audit dates) we should avoid scheduling automated rotations or simulated failovers.

I copied Ben and Irene to confirm the technical specifics below and to attach the internal runbook excerpt. If this looks good I can produce a short attestation and a one-page annex that can be appended to your SOW.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- operator_rotation_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet - rotation windows, token TTLs, KMS/HSM flows)
- standby_swarm_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpt - pages 1-12)
- access-approval-form.docx (stub for customer sign-off)

From: Sara Connors <sara.connors@aurumhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator credential rotation & standby swarm plan

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — we've started a review with our security ops leads. A couple of immediate clarifications:

- Break-glass window: our policy requires the shortest practical window; 2 hours is preferred for production clusters unless explicitly authorized for longer by our CISO. Can Redwood support 2-hour default for break-glass tokens and still meet the operator workflow you describe?

- Escalation / evacuation: we need explicit language on the physical operator evacuation procedure and evidence that on-prem operator access requires a signed escort request when on site. The runbook mentions escorting but doesn't include the escort request form.

- Audit trail: we need confirmation that all rotation and lease events are recorded to the local telemetry store and an option to forward those logs to our SIEM (Splunk) in near-real time (within 90s).

Also copying procurement (jacob.myers@procurecorp.com) for timing — we are aiming to have a procurement packet completed before the end of March.

Regards,
Sara Connors
Security Operations Lead, Aurum Health
security@aurumhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Re: Operator credential rotation & standby swarm plan

Hannah — forwarding Aurum's clarifications. Inline notes below.

> Sara: "Can Redwood support 2-hour default for break-glass tokens and still meet the operator workflow you describe?"
- Ben: yes. We can change default lease TTL to 2h for production-only policies. Implementation: vault lease manager supports TTL ranges; set default TTL=2h with a maximum re-issue of 8h pending CISO approval. Also add a mandatory justification field captured on request.

> Sara: "Escalation / evacuation: need explicit language on physical operator evacuation procedure and escort request form."
- Irene: runbook v2 has the prose but not a form. I can generate an Escort Request PDF that includes operator name, badge number, escort start/end times, and justification stamp. We'll attach as a new artifact. For air-gapped installs, the form will include a chain-of-custody token (HOTP-based) validated against the on-prem HSM.

> Sara: "Audit trail: confirm rotation and lease events are recorded locally and forwardable to Splunk within 90s."
- Ben: our telemetry agent writes a local event and ships via a signed-forwarder; typical latency to a customer SIEM over a dedicated egress is ~30-60s. We will include an SLA line: max 90s per event for forwarding; include jitter stats in appendix.

Action items (internal):
- Irene: create Escort Request PDF and add chain-of-custody section for air-gapped installs. Due: Mon 2026-03-16.
- Ben: update operator_rotation_matrix.xlsx default TTL and add explicit telemetry forwarding SLA note. Due: Mon 2026-03-16.
- Hannah/Marissa: prepare one-page annex for SOW with the break-glass defaults and attestations. Due: Tue 2026-03-17.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator credential rotation & standby swarm plan

Sara / Aurum Security team — thanks for the review and the timeline note. Below is our consolidated response and the next steps we propose.

1) Break-glass window and lease TTLs
- We will set the default break-glass lease TTL to 2 hours for production environments. Extension beyond 2h requires a CISO-signed override; the override will be recorded in the access-approval-form.docx (we'll add an audit-signature field).

2) Escort / evacuation procedure
- We've created an Escort Request PDF and embedded it in the runbook. For air-gapped installations the escort flow uses a HOTP chain-of-custody token validated against the on-prem HSM. The runbook section 4.2 now includes: steps for escort approval, operator badge revocation, physical escort checklist, and post-evacuation account suspension flow.

3) Audit trail & SIEM forwarding
- Agent will emit signed rotation/lease events to the local telemetry store; the signed-forwarder will forward to customer SIEM (Splunk) with a committed SLA of 90s max per event. We will provide a telemetry sample feed and a short test script for you to validate latency during your SOC tests.

4) Deliverables and timeline
- Updated artifacts attached (operator_rotation_matrix.xlsx v1.1, standby_swarm_runbook_v2b.pdf, access-approval-form.docx v1.2).
- Internal action items completed: Ben updated TTLs and telemetry SLA; Irene produced Escort Request form; Marissa and I prepared a one-page annex for your SOW.

Next steps we propose:
- Aurum: confirm acceptance of 2-hour break-glass default and your preferred date for the SOC test window (we recommend Mar 24–25, 2026).
- Procurement (Jacob): if procurement is ready, we'll attach the one-page annex to the SOW and issue a DocuSign envelope for access approvals. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-ACCESS-APPROVAL-2026

If that all looks good I'll circulate a signed attestation and the annex for your legal team.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the escort flow.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachments:

- standby_swarm_runbook_v2b.pdf (runbook pages 1-15; new escort form inserted on p9)
- access-approval-form.docx (v1.2; includes override/audit signature fields)
